definition: The set of things you normally do each day.
business_context_example: My daily routine survives holidays; my good intentions don't.

definition: To keep doing something you decided to do.
business_context_example: I stuck to it for nine weeks, then one busy Monday broke the chain.

definition: To return to an old bad habit after stopping.
business_context_example: I fell off the wagon in December, like everyone else.
translation_bg: да се върна към стар навик

definition: To return to a good habit or plan after a break.
business_context_example: One bad week doesn't matter if you get back on track.
translation_bg: да се върна в правия път

definition: To repeat something until it becomes automatic.
business_context_example: You build a habit by making it small enough to be boring.

definition: To relax gradually at the end of the day.
business_context_example: I wind down with a book, not with the news.

definition: To stop feeling worried or tense.
business_context_example: It takes me about forty minutes to unwind after a hard call.

definition: To go to bed earlier than usual.
business_context_example: Get an early night before the interview, it shows on your face.

definition: To stay in bed later than usual in the morning.
business_context_example: Saturday is the only day I have a lie-in.

definition: To sleep longer than you intended.
business_context_example: I overslept and missed the first half of the training.

definition: Someone who feels most awake late at night.
business_context_example: She's a night owl, so we never book her for 8 am sessions.

definition: The habits that help you sleep well.
business_context_example: Good sleep hygiene starts two hours before bed, not at bedtime.

definition: Having slept enough to feel good.
business_context_example: Nobody makes good decisions when they aren't well rested.

definition: The amount of time spent looking at a phone or computer.
business_context_example: My screen time report on Sunday is always an unpleasant surprise.

definition: To stop using digital devices for a while.
business_context_example: We unplug completely for one weekend every month.

definition: A planned period without phones or social media.
business_context_example: A three-day digital detox showed me how often I reach for nothing.

definition: Endlessly reading bad news online.
business_context_example: Doomscrolling at midnight explains most of my bad mornings.

definition: An alert from an app or device.
business_context_example: I turned off every notification except calls, and nothing broke.

definition: Time when you are not working and can rest.
business_context_example: Downtime isn't laziness, it's the part where you recover.

definition: To rest until you feel energetic again.
business_context_example: Two days in the mountains recharge me more than a week on a beach.

definition: Time spent alone doing what you want.
business_context_example: Half an hour of me time before the family wakes up changes the day.

definition: Looking after your own health and wellbeing.
business_context_example: Self-care is mostly sleep, water and saying no, not candles.

definition: To deal with pressure so it doesn't damage you.
business_context_example: Learning to manage stress did more for my health than the gym.

definition: Feeling there is too much to handle.
business_context_example: I felt overwhelmed until I wrote all of it on one page.

definition: Mental capacity to think about something.
business_context_example: I don't have the headspace for that decision today.

definition: To decide what you will and won't accept from others.
business_context_example: Setting boundaries at work felt rude for exactly two weeks.

definition: To refuse a request politely.
business_context_example: Learning to say no is the cheapest time-management tool there is.

definition: To start doing something for enjoyment.
business_context_example: He picked up a hobby at 45 and made friends for the first time in years.

definition: To meet or talk after not seeing each other for a while.
business_context_example: We catch up with friends on the first Thursday of every month.

definition: To arrange something for the future.
business_context_example: Make plans on Monday or the weekend disappears by itself.

definition: To decide not to do something you arranged.
business_context_example: Cancelling plans twice in a row is a signal, not a schedule problem.

definition: To spend time with other people for pleasure.
business_context_example: I socialise less in winter and feel it by February.
translation_bg: да общувам, да излизам с хора

definition: Time given fully to someone, without distractions.
business_context_example: Twenty minutes of quality time beats three hours on the same sofa.

definition: To work for a good cause without being paid.
business_context_example: She volunteers at the animal shelter two Saturdays a month.

definition: To remove things you don't need from a space.
business_context_example: We decluttered the flat and gave away nine bags.

definition: A thorough cleaning of the whole home.
business_context_example: The spring clean took a weekend and felt like a holiday.

definition: To spend no more money than you earn.
business_context_example: Living within your means is dull advice that quietly works.

definition: To keep money aside for something specific.
business_context_example: We're saving up for a proper holiday instead of three short ones.

definition: Work done for extra money alongside your main job.
business_context_example: Her side hustle earns less than her job and teaches her more.

definition: The regular journey between home and work.
business_context_example: A 50-minute commute each way is 400 hours a year.

definition: To do your job from your house.
business_context_example: I work from home on Tuesdays and get more done before ten.

definition: To stop thinking about work.
business_context_example: I can't switch off if my laptop is in the bedroom.

definition: To stop an activity for a short rest.
business_context_example: Take a break every 90 minutes and the afternoon stops being a fight.

definition: To move to live in a different place.
business_context_example: They relocated to a smaller city and cut their rent in half.
translation_bg: да се преместя да живея другаде

definition: To become comfortable in a new place or situation.
business_context_example: Give yourself three months to settle in before judging a new city.

definition: To decide clearly what you want to achieve.
business_context_example: Set goals you could explain to a ten-year-old.

definition: Becoming better as a person over time.
business_context_example: Personal growth is mostly doing uncomfortable things on purpose.

phrase: step out of your comfort zone
definition: To do something that feels risky or unfamiliar.
business_context_example: Speaking English in the meeting was stepping out of her comfort zone.
audio_text: step out of your comfort zone
translation_bg: да изляза от зоната си на комфорт

definition: To protect time for your own needs.
business_context_example: Make time for yourself before the calendar takes all of it.
translation_bg: да отделя време за себе си

definition: To do things at a calmer pace.
business_context_example: I had to slow down before I understood what was actually urgent.
